findings.evidence: {schedulesError || sectionsError ? (<div className="table-card">Could not load. Check your connection and try again.<button onClick={() => fetchSchedules()}>Retry</button>...) — two independent sources (fetchSchedules, useAcademicLogic.jsx:475, and fetchSections, useAcademicLogic.jsx:271) collapse into one message, and the only retry re-runs fetchSchedules; fetchSections is not even destructured on line 49.

findings.evidence: {schedulesLoading ? (...) : activeSubjects.map(subject => { ... })} — the ternary has a loading branch and a mapped branch and no branch for activeSubjects.length === 0, so an empty subject registry renders the <thead> on lines 190-194 over an empty <tbody>.
findings.message: When no active subjects exist the schedule table falls through to a bare header row over blank space, with no zero-result branch at all.

findings.evidence: <div className="modal-overlay open" onClick={closeScheduleOverlay}><div className="modal"> — the schedule form mounts with no role="dialog", no initial focus on the teacher select, no Escape binding and no restoration of focus to the Add button on line 225 that opened it.
findings.message: The schedule modal never takes, holds or returns focus, so keyboard users remain outside the dialog they just opened.

findings.evidence: const closeSectionOverlay = (e) => { if (e.target === e.currentTarget) closeSectionModal(); }; — closeSectionModal is setSectionModal(null) (useAcademicLogic.jsx:302); secName, secGrade, secAdviser and secCapacity are never consulted on the way out.
findings.message: Clicking the backdrop throws away everything typed into the section form without asking.

findings.evidence: Three buttons in the trailing cell all read className="icon-action": class list (line 66), Edit (line 67) and Delete (line 68) — the delete, which drops the section's class list and schedules, is styled no differently from the other two.
findings.message: The section Delete button is weighted identically to its two safe siblings in the same row, with no use of the red .archive-action variant.

findings.evidence: <div className="modal-overlay open" onClick={closeSectionOverlay}><div className="modal"> at line 77, and the class-list overlay at line 118, both mount with no role="dialog", no focus call, no key handler and no focus restoration on close.
findings.message: Both section overlays leave focus on the page behind them, so tabbing walks straight out of the dialog and nothing returns focus when it closes.

findings.evidence: <button className="icon-action" aria-label={`Remove ${c.name} from this section`} onClick={() => removeStudentFromSection(c.id)}> — removeStudentFromSection (useAcademicLogic.jsx:452) deletes the row then calls loadClassList, which re-renders the table without that row; nothing anywhere moves focus.
findings.message: Activating a row's Remove button unmounts the button that holds focus and nothing restores focus, so a keyboard user is dropped back to the document body inside an open modal.

findings.evidence: `Portal Name` beside ``, and the same span pattern for Academic Year (line 36) and Quarter (line 40)
findings.message: The settings fields are labelled with plain spans rather than associated label elements, so the inputs and selects have no accessible name.

findings.evidence: const closeSubjectOverlay = (e) => { if (e.target === e.currentTarget) closeSubjectModal(); }; — the backdrop handler and the Cancel button (line 89) both call closeSubjectModal, which is just setSubjectModal(null) (useAcademicLogic.jsx:60). Neither reads sName/sCode to see whether anything was typed.
findings.message: A stray backdrop click silently discards a half-filled subject form, because the dismissal path and the cancel path are the same unconditional unmount with no dirty check.

findings.evidence: <button className="icon-action" aria-label={`Delete ${s.code}`} ...><Trash2/></button> sits beside the Edit button on line 56 with the identical className="icon-action" — while AdminDashboard.jsx:249 defines .archive-action { color: var(--red); } and SchedulesTab.jsx:217 uses "icon-action archive-action" for its delete.
findings.message: The permanent-delete button carries exactly the same class, size and colour as the Edit button next to it, ignoring the destructive .archive-action variant the design system already provides.

findings.evidence: <div className="modal-overlay open" onClick={closeSubjectOverlay}><div className="modal"> — no role="dialog", no aria-modal, no autoFocus on the first input, no Escape handler and no focus restoration; a grep for autoFocus, focus(), Escape or keydown across pages/dashboards/admin returns nothing.
findings.message: The subject modal opens without moving focus into it, without trapping focus inside it, and without returning focus to the button that opened it.
